claims.claim: The 2021 demographic model estimated an early split around 12,000 BP with a wide confidence interval.
Early cultivated cannabis was probably multipurpose; stronger fiber/drug divergence appears around 4,000 BP.
Zhuzhai preserves very early cannabis seed evidence consistent with possible cultivation.
Cannabis phytoliths occur at two Shandong sites dating about 4,500–3,400 BP.
Shandong cannabis phytoliths exceed 50% ubiquity and commonly co-occur with staple crops.
Eurasian cannabis use/spread has a complex archaeological record rather than one simple route.
A rise in East Asian seed records around 5,000–4,000 cal BP may relate to exchange/migration networks.
Fiber/drug groups show differing selection signals involving branching, flowering, stem biology and chemical production.
Cannabinoid-related genetic machinery bears marks of domestication/breeding.
Haimenkou yielded >800 cannabis grains, ~700 from one context, dating about 1650–400 BCE.
Haimenkou seed measurements mostly overlap modern psychoactive/fiber ranges and fit diversification, not a clean binary.
Jirzankal braziers around 500 BCE preserve cannabis biomarkers including CBN.
Jirzankal supports deliberate ritual burning of cannabis with relatively high psychoactive compounds.
Jirzankal does not determine the exact breeding pathway that produced potent plants.
Yanghai preserves ~2,700-year-old cannabis with chemical/genetic evidence of psychoactive potential.
The 2025 Nature pangenome used 193 genomes from 144 biological samples and found extensive variation/hybridization.
The 2025 authors conclude cannabis diversity remains partly characterized and wild Asian relatives are likely.
